title: Transient commitment smoothing and deferment acceptance criteria
creator: Jorge Marquez
description:
PRD summary: Define a transient commitment smoothing mechanism that allows customers with recurring compute/usage commitments to absorb short spikes without immediate hard overage billing. The feature will: (1) allow short-term borrowing against future committed credits up to a capped percentage, (2) present deferred usage as a distinct line-item in the Console and on invoices, (3) reconcile deferred usage automatically at settlement windows with clear rollback rules, and (4) provide observability and audit trails for finance and support teams.

Scope clarifications and boundaries: This work covers product requirements, acceptance criteria, and billing test cases for the hosted API + Dedicated tiers. It does NOT include the Private on-prem installer changes or changes to partner billing integrations. Implementation will require coordination with Finance (invoice line-items), Billing (metering and settlement jobs), Console (UI and user notifications), and Backend (usage ledger and reconciliation job).

Key assumptions: customers will accept a time-limited deferred charge visible in the console; deferred usage will be limited to avoid revenue leakage; reconciliation occurs automatically at monthly settlement unless customer has explicitly elected alternate settlement.

Primary goals: reduce false-positive overage incidents, smooth customer experience during short transients, reduce support tickets from unexpected overage billing, and maintain clear, auditable financial treatment for deferred usage.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Borrow cap - For any customer plan with a recurring monthly commitment, the system allows transient borrowing up to 20% of that month's remaining commitment or 50k token-equivalent (whichever is lower) for a maximum of 72 continuous hours.

AC-2: Visibility - When borrowing occurs a ‘Deferred usage’ line appears in the Console per-caller and per-route, with a timestamped breakdown and the original vs. borrowed units. Console link: https://console.redwood.ai/billing/deferred-usage (mock route for QA).

AC-3: Notifications - Customers receive an in-console banner and email when deferred usage is engaged and again 24 hours before the smoothing window expires. Email template located at Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/DEFERMENT-EMAIL-TEMPLATE.

AC-4: Automatic reconciliation - At monthly settlement, deferred usage is either charged (if remaining commitment exhausted) or returned to the customer as a credit if actual usage falls below the committed level. Reconciliation math must match Finance spec v1.2 (Drive doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/finance-specs).

AC-5: Billing line-item - Invoices must include a discrete line for ‘Deferred usage (smoothing)’ with the original timestamp of the borrow event and the settlement decision (charged/refunded). GitHub PR for invoice schema: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/314.

AC-6: Audit logs - Each borrow, extend, reconcile or rollback action emits an audit event retained for 13 months and queryable via the Admin Audit API. Sample audit payload and query examples in docs (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/billing-audit-playbook.

AC-7: Safety and caps - System must never allow borrowed usage to exceed the plan owner's global account cap; attempts beyond this should trigger a graceful fallback to soft-throttle (not hard-terminate) and a customer-visible notice.

AC-8: Edge case - If a customer downgrades or cancels the plan mid-smoothing window, deferred usage is reconciled pro-rata at the effective downgrade timestamp and the customer receives an immediate invoice adjustment or credit memo as per Finance policy.

AC-9: Metric validation - For the pilot cohort (10 customers), deferred borrow events should reduce support overage tickets by at least 30% vs. baseline over a 30d window. Metrics dashboard: internal Grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/usage-smoothing.

AC-10: Security & multitenancy - No KV cache, model traces, or PII are stored in the deferred usage records beyond aggregated token counts and route IDs; cross-tenant leakage must be validated in a security checklist sign-off (see security checklist doc in Confluence).
comments: 2025-02-18 Jorge Marquez: Initial draft PRD created and shared with Finance + Billing. Raised open question about revenue recognition windows; flagged for Finance input.

2025-02-19 Asha Patel: Engineering feasibility notes received - suggested implementation via an intermediate 'deferred ledger' table to avoid modifying existing metering pipeline. Pros: minimal change to real-time path. Con: additional reconciliation job required.

2025-02-20 Priya Shah (Finance): Recommended cap of 20% and 72h smoothing window to balance customer goodwill with revenue protection. Requested invoice line-item to include original timestamp and settlement decision.

2025-02-21 Dan Wu (Billing): Proposed approach for settlement - run daily partial reconciliation and final monthly settlement. Raised concern about invoice churn; suggested grouping deferred events into a single monthly settlement line when possible.

2025-02-23 Design review (Melissa Huang): Reviewed Console banners and line-item UI. Requested a tooltip explaining 'Deferred usage' and acceptance criteria for admin-level toggles. Design mock: https://drive.google.com/file/d/console-mock.

2025-02-24 Engineering triage (Asha): Scope bumped to include Dedicated tier because Dedicated customers reported support pains from surprise overages. Added 2 points to estimate. Engineering will create a safe flag to disable smoothing per-account.

2025-02-25 PM decision: Accept Finance cap recommendation. Next steps: create engineering spike to prototype deferred ledger, UX mock finalization, and billing schema PR. Owner: Asha. QA owner: Ravi Patel.
